title: Ukrainian ground robots and drones may have taken a Russian position with no infantry and no Ukrainian losses; the location, date, unit and prisoner count are undisclosed
summary: President Zelenskyy said on 13 April 2026 that Ukrainian ground robots and drones had taken an enemy position with no infantry and no Ukrainian losses; no source has verified the claim.
account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said that ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek reports that he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica reports that the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast the previous year. Politico describes the robots as “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”. No outlet has since confirmed the place, date or unit of the April operation. Unmanned assaults spread later in 2026: Forbes describes a fully unmanned assault by the 33rd Separate Assault Regiment near Dobropillya in July. In September the 3rd Army Corps said that its drones had dropped armed robots behind Russian lines in Operation Vivaldi.
purpose: Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicles and drones are built to carry out front-line missions in place of soldiers. Those missions include assaults, logistics and evacuation. Taking a position without exposing infantry is that purpose.
system: Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicles (Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia, as named by Zelenskyy) operating with aerial drones

ratings.reason: The President reports that his forces took an enemy position without infantry and without losses, a gain in what the force can do without exposing soldiers. The claim is unverified, and no source gives the place, date or unit.

ai_role.statement: No source describes an AI function in this operation. Politico says the ground robotic systems are “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”. Jacob Parakilas of RAND Europe writes in The Conversation that they are “mostly still remotely operated”. He says autonomy is limited to tasks such as highlighting identified enemy positions. The Debrief says it is unclear how much remote human control was involved at each stage. Politico separately notes a January 2026 case in which a DevDroid robot “equipped with artificial intelligence elements” took three prisoners, a different event.

fields.summary: President Zelenskyy said on 13 April 2026 that Ukrainian ground robots and drones had taken an enemy position with no infantry and no Ukrainian losses; no source has verified the claim.
fields.account: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave an Arms Makers' Day address on Monday 13 April 2026. “For the first time in the history of this war, an enemy position was taken exclusively by unmanned platforms — ground systems and drones,” he said. He added that “the occupiers surrendered, and the operation was carried out without infantry and without losses on our side” (Politico, Business Insider, Censor.NET). He said that ground robotic systems performed more than 22,000 missions on Ukraine's front line in the first three months of 2026. He named Ratel, TerMIT, Ardal, Rys, Zmiy, Protector and Volia. Newsweek reports that he did not say where the advance took place. No outlet gives a date, unit or prisoner count. Ars Technica reports that the claim is not independently verified and may refer to a 3rd Separate Assault Brigade action in Kharkiv Oblast the previous year. Politico describes the robots as “currently piloted by humans from a safe distance”. No outlet has since confirmed the place, date or unit of the April operation. Unmanned assaults spread later in 2026: Forbes describes a fully unmanned assault by the 33rd Separate Assault Regiment near Dobropillya in July. In September the 3rd Army Corps said that its drones had dropped armed robots behind Russian lines in Operation Vivaldi.
